symbols.note: copied by hand from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe). Methods with null address were listed by the Toolkit but the tool printed no game address for them. System index variable bg3_dx11.exe+0x60D979C; the game functions using the index are in the Toolkit line of the tool output. The does layer cites EoCServer.dll (Toolkit pseudo-code with real names) wherever bg3_dx11.exe functions were not individually mapped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Drains a queue of price requests kept at this+0x10 (by the name, filled by LEGACY_RequestSetBuybackPrice; that method was not read). For each queued entity that is alive it walks the entities of its stack with ForEachEntityInStack; the lambda puts each member into a set and, only the first time a member is seen, adds a component to it through the deferred command buffer and copies a two-byte value from the request into it. The component's type is not named in the lambda; SetTradeBuybackPriceRequestOneFrameComponent, the method's one-frame write, is the likely one. Then the queue is emptied.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0xF20A60 read (queue, alive check, ForEachEntityInStack, queue cleared); its lambda EoCServer.dll+0xF208D0 read (set insert, AddComponent through helper EoCServer.dll+0xF1DD80, two-byte copy)
does.check: not checkable live: the claim is not settled enough to state an expectation (see unknown)

does.text: Works through five queries, resolved: (1) items on which an inventory MemberAdded event and a SetTradeBuybackPriceRequestOneFrameComponent were just added, with their ownership (OwneeCurrent, OwneeHistory) and optional TradeBuybackData/inventory Owner; (2) items on which an EntitySplit event was just added (a stack split); (3) eoc::character::TradingComponent removed from an entity with eoc::PlayerComponent (a trade ended); (4) items with MemberAdded, TradeBuybackData and OwneeCurrent; (5) all items with TradeBuybackData. In the split pass, when the owners before and after differ and one side is a player (HasComponent eoc::PlayerComponent, EoCServer.dll+0x336480) and a trader test (+0xF1EC70) passes, it writes the request's two-byte price and the two owner handles into a component obtained through +0xF1DCD0, and copies an existing TradeBuybackData into eoc::inventory::TradeBuybackDataComponent added on the entity (helper +0xF1DF70). Later passes remove TradeBuybackDataComponent when the item's recorded owner no longer matches (lines 640-691) and, in the last pass, from items once the trade is over (line 856). The exact pairing of these branches with the five queries was not followed to the end.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0xF20E40 named pseudo-code, keyhole reads at 167-305, 380-470, 515-545, 640-700, 840-860; queries DAT_18225b13c/b140/b144/b148/b14c resolved through their init functions; add helper +0xF1DF70 = SetupComponentFrameStorage (0x18 bytes) of DAT_1822401b8 = eoc::inventory::TradeBuybackDataComponent; +0xF1E400 = SetTradeBuybackPriceRequestOneFrameComponent; RemoveComponentUnchecked of DAT_1822401b8 at 691 and 856.
